messages.author: 678b515b89104b63
messages.subject: (mild) regularity conditions
parts:
Good evening,

I am new to R-INLA and novice in statistics. I was reading papers about INLA and they all state that, to use INLA, "(mild) regularity conditions" have to be met, but do not go into details about what it means. 
It is probably obvious to everyone here, but what does this mean? Does it have anything to do with making sure the precision matrix is positive definite? And how do I know if a function not listed in the latent models could meet those conditions?

Thank you very much for your help.

If it is something too long/complicated to explain on this board, I would appreciate a reference to this as I have googled this for hours and could not find an answer.
Again, thank you.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] (mild) regularity conditions
parts:
you can check this one,

http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0047259X12001297

and the intuition behind the approximations (which kind of say what
conditions you need to make them work),

https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.00860

or here, if you have access

http://www.annualreviews.org/journal/statistics


I would not worry to much. one need log likelihoods to be continous,
and two times derivative, preferably concave, and similar conditions
for the log priors.

H
